claims.text: The trip record shows the rider cancelled at 17:35:08, and the scheduled pickup time was 17:55:08 — that is 20 minutes before the scheduled time. Under POL-NS-10(b), a cancellation made more than platform_policy.advance_grace_before_scheduled_sec (900 seconds, i.e. 15 minutes) before trip_record.scheduled_at is not chargeable. The rider cancelled 1200 seconds before the scheduled time, which is more than the 900-second advance grace, so the cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full.

The trip record confirms the cancellation was made by the rider with reason code RIDER_CANCELLED, and the fare breakdown shows a cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 was charged. Under POL-NS-10(c), a cancellation fee charged on a cancellation that limb (a) or (b) makes non-chargeable is refunded in full with no driver compensation. The fee must be refunded.

The GPS trace shows the driver's track spans from 17:10:08 to 17:36:08, with the driver's minimum distance from the pickup pin being approximately 14,000 metres (14 km). The driver never came within the arrival radius of 50 metres for a STANDARD zone class, and indeed never came within 400 metres of the pickup pin. Under POL-NS-02, where the gps_trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes preceding the cancellation, the driver never arrived and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails. The fee is not chargeable.

The GPS trace shows the driver's longest qualifying in-geofence run was 0 seconds, with 0 qualifying fixes and 0 in-geofence intervals. Under POL-NS-06, where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force (180 seconds for STANDARD zone class), the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full. The driver never entered the geofence, so the dwell is zero and the fee must be refunded.

The trip record shows the driver was assigned at 17:10:08 with an ETA of 40 minutes, meaning the driver would not have arrived until approximately 17:50:08. The rider cancelled at 17:35:08, which is 15 minutes before the driver's estimated arrival. Under POL-NS-10(f), a rider's own cancellation after the grace period is chargeable EXCEPT where the driver had not arrived within 180 seconds of the first estimated arrival time shown to the rider. Here the driver had not arrived at all, and the cancellation was well before the estimated arrival time. The fee must be refunded.

The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02738-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0. Under POL-NS-06(i), a MISSING traffic_advisory makes limb (i) unavailable, and asserting it against a MISSING artifact triggers POL-NS-09 rather than exonerating anyone. The absence of any advisory covering the pickup road means there is no basis to accumulate dwell across separate intervals or to excuse any shortfall. The full refund stands.

The rider profile shows no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, and the driver profile shows disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0. Under POL-NS-09(c), escalation is triggered where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. That condition is not met here, so no escalation is warranted on that ground. The case can be decided on the merits.

The driver profile shows no_show_terminations_30d is 2 and completed_trips_30d is 90. Under POL-NS-07, the anti-farming check trips where no_show_terminations_30d is 4 or more AND the ratio to completed_trips_30d exceeds 0.08. Here the count is 2 (below 4) and the ratio is 0.022 (below 0.08), so the anti-farming check does not trip. However, this is context only — the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-10(b) regardless of the driver's profile.

claims.text: The rider cancelled this trip herself, 25 minutes after the driver was assigned and 20 minutes before the scheduled pickup time, and the trip record shows cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED with cancelled_by RIDER. Under POL-NS-10(f) a rider's own cancellation after the grace period is chargeable at the platform's cancellation fee whether or not the driver had arrived, and none of limb (f)'s four exceptions is shown on this record: the driver began moving toward the pickup within the grace (driver_en_route event at 17:10:16, six seconds after assignment), the driver's ETA was 40 minutes against a scheduled pickup 45 minutes out, there is no chat message asking the rider to cancel (the chat log is empty), and no vehicle or driver mismatch is recorded.

The cancellation was not within the match grace: the trip was accepted at 17:10:08 and cancelled at 17:35:08, 1500 seconds later, far beyond the 180 second grace_after_match_sec in force for this trip. POL-NS-10(a) therefore does not make the fee non-chargeable.

The cancellation was not within the advance-booking grace either: the trip was scheduled for 17:55:08 and cancelled at 17:35:08, only 1200 seconds before the scheduled time, well inside the 900 second advance_grace_before_scheduled_sec window. POL-NS-10(b) therefore does not make the fee non-chargeable, and the rider's own claim that she cancelled 'twenty minutes before the pickup time' is exactly the fact that defeats her.

The fee charged reconciles with the policy figure: the fare breakdown shows a cancellation_fee of SGD 4.50 and total_charged of SGD 4.50, which equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50 for this trip. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the ledger notes confirm the lines reconcile to total_charged.

The rider's own device was at the pickup point at the moment of cancellation: the rider track carries a single fix at 17:35:48, 3.93 m from the pickup pin, stationary at 0.0 km/h. The rider was not stranded or mislocated; she was at the pin and cancelled anyway. This is not a POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance case and not a POL-NS-04 coordination-failure case.

The rider's claim that she was charged despite cancelling in good time is not supported by any locating or coordinating message: the chat log holds zero messages, first_message_at and last_message_at are null, and trip_record.chat_message_count is 0. POL-NS-04 limb (a) requires at least one locating or coordinating message from the rider during the waiting window, and there is none, so the rider-exonerating clause cannot run.

The driver's track shows 157 fixes at 10 second cadence with 100 percent coverage and no gaps, running from 17:10:08 to 17:36:08, and the driver was en route from six seconds after assignment. The driver performed the trip he accepted; the loss he bears from a late rider cancellation is real and the fee is what compensates it.

The driver's anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by completed_trips_30d of 90 is 0.022, below the 0.08 rate. Compensation is therefore payable and not withheld. I note that driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags is 1, but that is a lifetime counter and POL-NS-07 and POL-GEN-01 forbid substituting it for the trailing-30-day figure.

The rider's profile shows no pattern of abuse that would displace the fee: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, below the POL-NS-09(d) threshold of 3, and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so POL-NS-09(c) does not engage. No escalation trigger is present on this record.

I concede that the driver never arrived at the pickup point and that POL-NS-01 is not satisfied on this record: the trip record carries no 'arrived' event, arrived_at is null, and the derived arrival block shows zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds against a 180 second minimum dwell. The driver's fixes sit between roughly 14 km and 40 km from the pin throughout. The fee therefore cannot stand on POL-NS-01, and the driver's compensation cannot be founded on POL-NS-07's primary route.

I also concede that POL-NS-10(g) does not apply: that limb requires the rider to cancel after the driver has arrived under POL-NS-02 and after the in-geofence dwell has exceeded free_wait_sec, and on this record the driver never arrived. The fee stands, if it stands at all, on POL-NS-10(f) alone, and the driver's payout cannot be routed through POL-NS-07's limb (g) gateway.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload, so POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and no accumulated-dwell argument can be made on the driver's side. I cite the absence rather than assert against it, as POL-NS-06 requires.

ruling.explanation:
Rider — the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on 10 Aug 2026 is refunded to you in full. Driver — no compensation is payable on this trip.

The booking was an advance (scheduled) trip. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02738) shows it was accepted at 17:10:08 and scheduled for pickup at 17:55:08, and the rider cancelled at 17:35:08 — 1,200 seconds (20 minutes) before the scheduled time. POL-NS-10(b) provides that, for a scheduled trip, a cancellation made more than the advance grace of 900 seconds (15 minutes) before the scheduled time is not chargeable, and 1,200 seconds is more than 900 seconds. POL-NS-10(c) then requires the SGD 4.50 fee to be refunded in full with no driver compensation. The refunded amount is the cancellation-fee line of the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02738: cancellation_fee SGD 4.50, total_charged SGD 4.50), which matches platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50. The fare lines reconcile, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect — but a correctly stated fee can still be non-chargeable, and this one is.

Driver's arguments. Your claim that the rider's own cancellation is chargeable under POL-NS-10(f) fails because limb (f) reaches only cancellations that fall outside both protective windows, limbs (a) and (b); this cancellation falls inside limb (b)'s protection. Your reading of limb (b) — that a cancellation 1,200 seconds before the scheduled time is 'well inside' a 900-second window — reverses the test: 1,200 is more than 900, so the fee is not chargeable, and the rider's own statement that she cancelled 'twenty minutes before' is the fact that defeats the charge. You are right that limb (a) does not protect the rider (the cancellation was 1,500 seconds after acceptance, past the 180-second match grace) and that the fee reconciles, but neither point helps once limb (b) applies. Your no-show case under POL-NS-01 is not made out: there is no 'arrived' event, arrived_at is null, the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02738) keeps the driver's fixes roughly 14 km or more from the pick-up pin, and the qualifying in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second free-wait minimum — a point both sides accept. Because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full and POL-NS-10(g) does not apply (the rider cancelled before any arrival), POL-NS-07 cannot pay you: the anti-farming check does not trip (2 no-show terminations in 30 days against 90 completed trips, ratio 0.022), but no compensation arises in any event, and the driver-side loss argument does not create one where the clause's gateway is unmet.

Rider's other points. POL-NS-02 (the driver never entered the 50 m arrival radius), POL-NS-06 (zero dwell against the 180-second minimum) and POL-NS-04 (the chat log is empty, so no unanswered locating message) all point the same way or are moot; none of them changes the outcome, which POL-NS-10(b) decides. The rider's passing reference to POL-NS-10(f)'s ETA exception does not need to be reached, for the same reason limb (f) does not apply at all.

No escalation. Confidence is 0.92, above the 0.70 floor. The deciding facts — the scheduled time, the acceptance time, the cancellation time and the fee — are carried by EV-TRIP-02738 and EV-FARE-02738, each at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02738-01, weight 0.0) is not relied on, because POL-NS-10(b) does not require it, so it neither caps confidence nor triggers escalation; the GPS trace is complete (157 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, rider track present) and is not impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d). Neither profile shows counterparty disputes, no abuse threshold is met, and the two admissible instruments do not contradict each other. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes automatically.

ruling.explanation: To both parties. This was an advance (scheduled) booking: the trip was accepted at 17:10:08 for a 17:55:08 pickup, and the rider cancelled at 17:35:08 under reason code RIDER_CANCELLED. The cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 was charged and is now refunded in full. Decision: FULL_REFUND of SGD 4.50, with no driver compensation. Why the fee does not stand: POL-NS-10(b) provides that on a scheduled trip a cancellation made MORE than the advance grace of 900 seconds (15 minutes) before the scheduled pickup is not chargeable. The rider cancelled 1200 seconds (20 minutes) before 17:55:08, which is more than the 900-second grace, so the cancellation falls inside the free-cancellation window, and POL-NS-10(c) requires the whole fee back with no driver compensation. The trip was accepted 2700 seconds before the scheduled time, well outside the 900-second window, so the shorter 180-second match grace in limb (a) does not apply either. The driver's argument that 1200 seconds is 'inside' the 900-second window is rejected: 1200 exceeds 900, so the cancellation was early enough to be free, and his POL-NS-10(f) argument does not reach these facts, because (f) makes a rider's own cancellation chargeable only once the grace in (a) or (b) has run out - that is, within 15 minutes of the scheduled pickup - which this cancellation was not. The same result follows independently on the driver's side of the case. There is no 'arrived' event and arrived_at is null; the GPS trace places the driver between about 14 km and 40 km from the pickup pin throughout, with zero in-geofence fixes and zero qualifying dwell against the 180-second free waiting period. POL-NS-01 therefore fails at limbs (a), (b) and (c) - as the driver's own brief concedes - and POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 each require the cancellation fee to be refunded in full. POL-NS-01 limb (d) would fail too, the trip having been cancelled by the rider rather than terminated by the driver for a no-show. Driver compensation: none. POL-NS-10(c), POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 each bar it, and POL-NS-07's payout route is not reached because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full and POL-NS-10(g) does not apply (the driver never arrived). The anti-farming check does not trip in any event (no_show_terminations_30d 2, below 4; 2/90 = 0.022, below 0.08), so no escalation packet is produced; the lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags is context only and was not used. Evidence and weight: the deciding facts - the cancellation timestamps and reason code, and the driver's position - are carried by EV-TRIP-02738 and EV-GPS-02738, each fully admissible at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and confidence 0.92 sits below it. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02738-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries nothing; no part of this refund rests on it, and the rider's POL-NS-06 shortfall argument is reached on the GPS alone. The fare line of SGD 4.50 reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. On the remaining points: the rider was at the pin (3.93 m) at cancellation and the chat log is empty, so this is neither a POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance case nor a POL-NS-04 coordination-failure case - the rider simply does not need either clause, because the fee fails on the cancellation timing and on the driver's non-arrival. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the trip record and GPS agree rather than contradict, there are no same-party disputes in the trailing 90 days, the anti-farming check is clear, and the deciding facts are carried by weight-1.0 artifacts. No clause produces a referral, so the referrals list is empty. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so the refund executes automatically; this is a provisional ruling and either party may appeal it once within 30 days.

ruling.explanation:
This was an advance booking and the rider's dispute is upheld: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full.

The controlling figures are in EV-TRIP-02738. The trip was accepted at 17:10:08, was scheduled for pickup at 17:55:08, and was cancelled by the rider at 17:35:08 — 1200 seconds before the scheduled time. POL-NS-10(b) provides that a cancellation made MORE than the advance grace of 900 seconds before scheduled_at is not chargeable. 1200 seconds is more than 900 seconds, so the cancellation falls inside the protected advance window and the fee is not chargeable. POL-NS-10(c) then requires the fee charged to be refunded in full with no driver compensation. EV-FARE-02738 shows cancellation_fee = SGD 4.50 and total_charged = SGD 4.50, matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so the amount refunded is SGD 4.50 and there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect.

The Driver Advocate argued the fee stands on POL-NS-10(f). It does not. Limb (f) makes chargeable only a rider cancellation that falls AFTER the grace in limb (a) or (b); this cancellation falls inside the (b) advance grace, so (f) never engages and none of its exceptions need be reached. The Driver Advocate's companion claim that POL-NS-10(b) does not apply because the cancellation was "only 1200 seconds" before the scheduled time is rejected on the arithmetic: 1200 seconds is greater than the 900-second advance grace, not less. The driver's concessions that he never arrived (no 'arrived' event, arrived_at null, zero qualifying in-geofence fixes) are accepted and confirm the fee cannot be supported under POL-NS-01, and his POL-NS-07 compensation route fails with it. The Driver Advocate's POL-NS-07 anti-farming claim (no_show_terminations_30d = 2, ratio 0.022, both below threshold) and POL-NS-09 no-escalation claim are accepted.

The Rider Advocate's POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 claims (driver never within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, zero in-geofence dwell) are accepted but add nothing to the dispositive POL-NS-10(b) ground; the rider's limb (f) exception claim is not reached because (f) does not apply.

No escalation trigger fires under POL-NS-09. Confidence is above the 0.70 floor; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0; the anti-farming check does not trip; and the deciding facts rest on artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0 (EV-TRIP-02738, EV-FARE-02738), so no POL-GEN-02(2) discount applies. No artifact below weight 1.0 is relied on for this ruling, so POL-GEN-02(3) narration is not engaged. No clause produces a referral: there is no 'arrived' event for POL-NS-05(ii) to record as false, and no driver no-show code for POL-NS-01's education referral. The monetary effect of SGD 4.50 does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so the refund executes automatically.

Step 1 discards: both traffic-advisory claims (RIDER and DRIVER) were discarded by the referee for citing the MISSING artifact EV-ADVIS-02738-01 (weight 0.0) without naming its issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. The referee's flag on the Driver Advocate's mention of driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags is noted only: that claim correctly treats the lifetime counter as context and does not rely on it.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your claim is upheld and the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full. This was an advance booking — the trip record shows the pickup scheduled for 17:55:08 — and you cancelled at 17:35:08, which is 1,200 seconds (20 minutes) before the scheduled time. POL-NS-10(b) makes a cancellation made more than platform_policy.advance_grace_before_scheduled_sec — 900 seconds (15 minutes), read from the platform policy in force on this trip — before the scheduled pickup non-chargeable, and POL-NS-10(c) requires the fee charged on such a cancellation to be refunded in full with no driver compensation. The SGD 4.50 shown as the cancellation-fee line in the fare breakdown is returned to you.

To the driver: your central argument reverses the arithmetic. You say the 1,200-second gap is 'well inside the 900-second window', but 1,200 seconds is MORE than 900 — the cancellation falls outside the chargeable window, so POL-NS-10(b) applies and makes the fee non-chargeable. For the same reason your POL-NS-10(f) argument does not bite: (f) charges only a rider cancellation made after the limb (a)/(b) grace, and this cancellation was made before the advance-booking grace expired, so (f) never reaches the fee. I accept your concession, which the record confirms, that you never arrived: the trip record carries no 'arrived' event (arrived_at is null), and the GPS trace places you between roughly 14 km and 40 km from the pickup pin throughout, with zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 s against the 180 s minimum dwell. POL-NS-01 therefore fails and there is no verified no-show, so no driver compensation is payable under POL-NS-07 — the anti-farming check does not trip in any event (no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below 4, and 2/90 = 0.022, below 0.08), but there is no qualifying no-show to compensate. Your remaining points are accepted but not decisive: the rider was at the pin (a single fix 3.93 m away at 17:35:48) and sent no locating message (the chat log is empty, so POL-NS-04 cannot run), but neither POL-NS-03 nor POL-NS-04 needs to decide this fee because POL-NS-10(b) already does. On the profiles, driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags was correctly identified by both sides as a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting for the citable trailing-window counters, and it played no part in this ruling.

On escalation and weight: no POL-NS-09 trigger fires. Confidence is above the 0.70 floor; the admissible artifacts do not contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; neither profile shows the abuse patterns (disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0; rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0); and the deciding fact — the cancellation timing against the scheduled time — rests on the trip record at weight 1.0, with the fare amount carried by the fare breakdown at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02738-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, but its absence carries no deciding fact here and does not impair this ruling. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 POL-GEN-05 execution threshold, so it executes automatically, subject to the appeal route in POL-GEN-04. Both parties receive this decision with the clauses and evidence relied on (POL-NS-10(b), POL-NS-10(c); EV-TRIP-02738, EV-FARE-02738).

ledger.claim: The trip record shows the rider cancelled at 17:35:08, and the scheduled pickup time was 17:55:08 — that is 20 minutes before the scheduled time. Under POL-NS-10(b), a cancellation made more than platform_policy.advance_grace_before_scheduled_sec (900 seconds, i.e. 15 minutes) before trip_record.scheduled_at is not chargeable. The rider cancelled 1200 seconds before the scheduled time, which is more than the 900-second advance grace, so the cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full.

The trip record confirms the cancellation was made by the rider with reason code RIDER_CANCELLED, and the fare breakdown shows a cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 was charged. Under POL-NS-10(c), a cancellation fee charged on a cancellation that limb (a) or (b) makes non-chargeable is refunded in full with no driver compensation. The fee must be refunded.

The GPS trace shows the driver's track spans from 17:10:08 to 17:36:08, with the driver's minimum distance from the pickup pin being approximately 14,000 metres (14 km). The driver never came within the arrival radius of 50 metres for a STANDARD zone class, and indeed never came within 400 metres of the pickup pin. Under POL-NS-02, where the gps_trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes preceding the cancellation, the driver never arrived and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails. The fee is not chargeable.

The GPS trace shows the driver's longest qualifying in-geofence run was 0 seconds, with 0 qualifying fixes and 0 in-geofence intervals. Under POL-NS-06, where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force (180 seconds for STANDARD zone class), the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full. The driver never entered the geofence, so the dwell is zero and the fee must be refunded.

The trip record shows the driver was assigned at 17:10:08 with an ETA of 40 minutes, meaning the driver would not have arrived until approximately 17:50:08. The rider cancelled at 17:35:08, which is 15 minutes before the driver's estimated arrival. Under POL-NS-10(f), a rider's own cancellation after the grace period is chargeable EXCEPT where the driver had not arrived within 180 seconds of the first estimated arrival time shown to the rider. Here the driver had not arrived at all, and the cancellation was well before the estimated arrival time. The fee must be refunded.

The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02738-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0. Under POL-NS-06(i), a MISSING traffic_advisory makes limb (i) unavailable, and asserting it against a MISSING artifact triggers POL-NS-09 rather than exonerating anyone. The absence of any advisory covering the pickup road means there is no basis to accumulate dwell across separate intervals or to excuse any shortfall. The full refund stands.

ledger.claim: The rider profile shows no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, and the driver profile shows disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0. Under POL-NS-09(c), escalation is triggered where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. That condition is not met here, so no escalation is warranted on that ground. The case can be decided on the merits.

The driver profile shows no_show_terminations_30d is 2 and completed_trips_30d is 90. Under POL-NS-07, the anti-farming check trips where no_show_terminations_30d is 4 or more AND the ratio to completed_trips_30d exceeds 0.08. Here the count is 2 (below 4) and the ratio is 0.022 (below 0.08), so the anti-farming check does not trip. However, this is context only — the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-10(b) regardless of the driver's profile.

The rider cancelled this trip herself, 25 minutes after the driver was assigned and 20 minutes before the scheduled pickup time, and the trip record shows cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED with cancelled_by RIDER. Under POL-NS-10(f) a rider's own cancellation after the grace period is chargeable at the platform's cancellation fee whether or not the driver had arrived, and none of limb (f)'s four exceptions is shown on this record: the driver began moving toward the pickup within the grace (driver_en_route event at 17:10:16, six seconds after assignment), the driver's ETA was 40 minutes against a scheduled pickup 45 minutes out, there is no chat message asking the rider to cancel (the chat log is empty), and no vehicle or driver mismatch is recorded.

The cancellation was not within the match grace: the trip was accepted at 17:10:08 and cancelled at 17:35:08, 1500 seconds later, far beyond the 180 second grace_after_match_sec in force for this trip. POL-NS-10(a) therefore does not make the fee non-chargeable.

The cancellation was not within the advance-booking grace either: the trip was scheduled for 17:55:08 and cancelled at 17:35:08, only 1200 seconds before the scheduled time, well inside the 900 second advance_grace_before_scheduled_sec window. POL-NS-10(b) therefore does not make the fee non-chargeable, and the rider's own claim that she cancelled 'twenty minutes before the pickup time' is exactly the fact that defeats her.

The fee charged reconciles with the policy figure: the fare breakdown shows a cancellation_fee of SGD 4.50 and total_charged of SGD 4.50, which equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50 for this trip. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the ledger notes confirm the lines reconcile to total_charged.

The rider's own device was at the pickup point at the moment of cancellation: the rider track carries a single fix at 17:35:48, 3.93 m from the pickup pin, stationary at 0.0 km/h. The rider was not stranded or mislocated; she was at the pin and cancelled anyway. This is not a POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance case and not a POL-NS-04 coordination-failure case.

The rider's claim that she was charged despite cancelling in good time is not supported by any locating or coordinating message: the chat log holds zero messages, first_message_at and last_message_at are null, and trip_record.chat_message_count is 0. POL-NS-04 limb (a) requires at least one locating or coordinating message from the rider during the waiting window, and there is none, so the rider-exonerating clause cannot run.

The driver's track shows 157 fixes at 10 second cadence with 100 percent coverage and no gaps, running from 17:10:08 to 17:36:08, and the driver was en route from six seconds after assignment. The driver performed the trip he accepted; the loss he bears from a late rider cancellation is real and the fee is what compensates it.

The driver's anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by completed_trips_30d of 90 is 0.022, below the 0.08 rate. Compensation is therefore payable and not withheld. I note that driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags is 1, but that is a lifetime counter and POL-NS-07 and POL-GEN-01 forbid substituting it for the trailing-30-day figure.

ledger.claim: The rider's profile shows no pattern of abuse that would displace the fee: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, below the POL-NS-09(d) threshold of 3, and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so POL-NS-09(c) does not engage. No escalation trigger is present on this record.

I concede that the driver never arrived at the pickup point and that POL-NS-01 is not satisfied on this record: the trip record carries no 'arrived' event, arrived_at is null, and the derived arrival block shows zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds against a 180 second minimum dwell. The driver's fixes sit between roughly 14 km and 40 km from the pin throughout. The fee therefore cannot stand on POL-NS-01, and the driver's compensation cannot be founded on POL-NS-07's primary route.

I also concede that POL-NS-10(g) does not apply: that limb requires the rider to cancel after the driver has arrived under POL-NS-02 and after the in-geofence dwell has exceeded free_wait_sec, and on this record the driver never arrived. The fee stands, if it stands at all, on POL-NS-10(f) alone, and the driver's payout cannot be routed through POL-NS-07's limb (g) gateway.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload, so POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and no accumulated-dwell argument can be made on the driver's side. I cite the absence rather than assert against it, as POL-NS-06 requires.
